_doc: Gate lifecycle metadata -- WR-000019 slice S5.

One entry per gate script actually wired in ops/config/hooks.json (35 gates as of 2026-08-27, down from 38 -- WR-000019 slice S3 retired canonical-edit-gate.py, git-writer-gate.py and staging-attribution-gate.py the same day; the count is re-derivable any time by walking that file the same way ops/hook-telemetry-rollup.py's wiring() does). A gate wired ONLY through .claude/settings.json (delegation-gate.py, worktree-self-plumb.py, machine-converge.py) is a different wiring surface and out of this slice's DoD wording -- it is not listed here.

failure_class   one line, what this gate exists to catch. Reused verbatim from ops/config/hook-catch-classes.json's catch_class where an entry already existed there (36 of 38); the two gaps (rule-pack-preuse-reselection.py, rule-pack-drift-gate.py) are new one-liners drawn from the gate's own docstring.

catch_metric    where a real catch is visible in a log already on disk, and the rule for recognizing one there. See ops/gate-lifecycle-report.py's module docstring for the exact evaluator per true_positive.kind.

review_date     a static calendar checkpoint (90 days from admission, uniform first pass -- provisional, like the rollup's BUDGET_MS). A downgrade/retirement PROPOSAL from the weekly report can and should trigger review earlier than this date; this date is the backstop for a gate the report never flags.

mode            enforcing | announce | shadow, matching ops/hook-meter-run.py's own register vocabulary (block/reopen vs announce vs silent). Determined from the gate's OWN source (a live sys.exit(2) / return 2 / {'decision':'block'} / permissionDecision deny-or-ask path reachable in current code == enforcing; a live additionalContext-only path == announce; no live surfaced effect == shadow), cross-checked against the two gates that self-declare shadow status in their own docstrings (rule-pack-preuse-reselection.py, rule-pack-drift-gate.py) and against the Stop-gate rationing CLAUDE.md and hook-meter-run.py's docstring both name (2026-08-16 chat-lint-gate.py, 2026-08-23 map-architecture/context-handoff/stale-claim/loose-work/unread-artifact-gate.py -- all demoted from blocking to announcing; only conduct-stop-gate.py, completion-evidence-gate.py and the execve'd drift-assertion-gate.py kept the ability to reopen a turn).

THIS FILE PROPOSES NOTHING BY ITSELF. ops/gate-lifecycle-report.py reads it plus the logs above and computes proposals; nothing here changes a gate's actual wiring or mode -- that stays a human/PR act.

drift-assertion-gate.py.failure_class: drift asserted at turn end without a record

catch_metric.rule_description: a hook-guard.log line 'drift-assertion-gate BLOCK hits=N' -- the gate actually reopened the turn over an unrecorded drift assertion. Unlike drift-claim-gate.py's log() (which prefixes every line with an ISO timestamp), this gate's own log() writes `f"drift-assertion-gate {line}\n"` with NO leading timestamp (checked 2026-08-27, hooks/drift-assertion-gate.py:118-119) -- so a windowed true-positive count cannot be computed from this log at all, and is reported as a data gap rather than guessed at zero.
catch_metric.note: same execve situation as drift-claim-gate.py (see its note: this gate never reaches out/hook-telemetry.jsonl either), PLUS its own hook-guard.log lines carry no timestamp -- a real observability gap in the gate's own logging, worth a follow-up, but hooks/*.py is out of this slice's scope to edit.

catch_metric.rule_description: a hook-guard.log line 'TS drift-claim-gate CONTEXT tool=... hits=N' -- the gate injected its verification reminder because a completion/drift claim needed a fresh record behind it.
catch_metric.note: run-record-gate.py execve's this gate, replacing the process before hook-meter-run.py's own telemetry write runs, so it never appears in out/hook-telemetry.jsonl (confirmed empty for hook== 'run-record-gate.py' during this slice's research). out/hook-guard.log is a plain-text log ('TS name VERDICT(class) detail' per line, no ts field to parse structurally) -- true_positive matches the line shape directly instead of a JSON field.
